newsitem.title: UK: UK POLICE ARREST MAN SUSPECTED OF OF MONEY LAUNDERING.
newsitem.headline: UK POLICE ARREST MAN SUSPECTED OF OF MONEY LAUNDERING.

text.p: British police confirmed on Wednesday that they had arrested a man on suspicion of money laundering but refused to say if he was linked to a German kidnapping case more than 20 years ago.

They issued a brief statement after the Munich state prosecutor's office said the man being held in a London police station was Dieter Zlof, who was convicted of kidnapping the son of a wealthy industrialist in 1976.

"Officers arrested a 54-year-old man in connection with suspected money and fraud offences," a police spokesman said after being inudated with telephone inquiries seeking confirmation that it was Zlof.

The Munich prosecutor's office said Zlof, who was on Tuesday arrested in possession of 10.7 million marks ($6.3 million), was trying to exchange part of the ransom money he obtained in the kidnapping.
The former car salesman was released from prison about a year ago after serving a 15-year sentence imposed in 1980 for the kidnapping of Richard Oetker.
Zlof has always maintained his innocence but had to complete his full sentence because he never revealed where the 21 million mark ransom received from Oetker's family was hidden.
Oetker was released shortly after the money was paid but was left disabled for life after being confined to a narrow box and sujected to electric shocks while he was held captive.
Banknotes from the ransom money began surfacing late last year in Germany and abroad. Only 42 of the 1,000 mark ($690) notes were retrieved after the kidnap.
In January German police arrested two people near Ludwigsburg in southern Germany and confiscated two notes that were once part of the ransom.
Zlof, who will remain under surveillance for five years, must report regularly to a probation officer in Germany.
